sections.eyebrow: Temperature Compensation and Output Units Explained
sections.title: Temperature Compensation and Output Units Explained
sections.tabSummary: What automatic compensation and multi-unit output actually solve
body: What automatic compensation and multi-format output actually solve for a portable density meter.

Density readings change with temperature, so a measurement taken on a warm sample in production and one taken later on a cooled sample in the lab can genuinely disagree, even if nothing about the sample itself has changed. That's a real problem for a handheld meter meant to be used wherever the sample happens to be, not just in a temperature-controlled lab.

Densito compensates for temperature automatically, so the reading reflects the sample's actual density rather than the temperature it happened to be measured at. Pairing that with output in specific gravity, Brix, API units, or other formats means the result comes out in whatever unit the process already works in, rather than requiring a manual conversion afterward.

sections.title: Automation and Compliance Explained
sections.tabSummary: What autosampling and LabX connectivity actually remove from routine testing
body: What autosampling and LabX connectivity actually remove from routine density testing.

Manual density testing depends on the operator to load each sample, correct for viscosity, and record the result correctly, and a lab running many samples a day repeats that dependency every single time. A bubble trapped in the measuring cell or an uncorrected viscous sample can quietly skew a result without ever being obvious to the operator.

Excellence D4 automates both problems: BubbleCheck™ catches trapped air before it affects the reading, automatic viscosity correction removes the manual adjustment, and the optional autosampler runs up to 303 samples without an operator loading each one by hand. LabX connectivity then carries that same automation into the compliance side, capturing results with a full audit trail rather than depending on manual transcription.
